definition_en: to pull something tight, to make a great effort, to injure a muscle, or pressure and worry
core_image: 一根绷到极限、纤维起了毛边的绳子
scene: 绳子在重物下绷得紧紧的。The rope strained under the weight.
sceneCN: 这里 strain 是「拉紧」（第 1 个义项）；句意：绳子在重物下绷得紧紧的。

senses.title: Pull tight
senses.definition: to pull something tight or stretch it hard
senses.definitionCN: 把某物拉紧或用力拉伸
senses.example: The rope strained under the weight.
senses.exampleCN: 绳子在重物下绷得紧紧的。
senses.why: This is the basic physical sense.
senses.whyCN: 这是最基本的物理义项。

senses.title: Try very hard
senses.definition: to make a great effort to do something
senses.definitionCN: 为做某事付出很大努力
senses.example: She strained to hear him.
senses.exampleCN: 她使劲去听他说的话。
senses.why: Tightening the body becomes effort.
senses.whyCN: 绷紧身体，引申为用力。

senses.title: Injure a muscle
senses.definition: to injure a muscle by pulling it too hard
senses.definitionCN: 因用力过度而拉伤肌肉
senses.example: He strained his back.
senses.exampleCN: 他拉伤了背。
senses.why: Too much pulling hurts the body.
senses.whyCN: 拉得过猛，身体就会受伤。

senses.title: Pressure and worry
senses.definition: pressure or worry caused by heavy demands
senses.definitionCN: 由沉重负担造成的压力或忧虑
senses.example: The strain of the journey tired them.
senses.exampleCN: 旅途的劳累让他们疲惫。
senses.why: Being pulled tight becomes being burdened.
senses.whyCN: 被拉紧，转指被压得紧绷。

intro.en: Strain comes from Latin stringere by way of French.
intro.cn: strain 经法语来自拉丁语 stringere。

items.en: Stringere meant to draw tight.
items.cn: stringere 意为拉紧。

items.en: Estraindre meant to press or tighten.
items.cn: estraindre 意为压紧或收紧。

items.en: Strain meant to stretch and to filter.
items.cn: strain 兼指拉伸与过滤。

items.en: Strain named effort and injury.
items.cn: strain 指用力与扭伤。

items.en: Strain named pressure and worry.
items.cn: strain 指压力与忧虑。

note.en: Strain is compared with look-alike words and with words for effort and pressure.
note.cn: 把 strain 与形近词以及表示用力与压力的词作比较。

entries.definition: to pull out to full length

normalIntro.en: Strain is what happens when the pull exceeds the strength.
normalIntro.cn: strain 就是拉力超过强度时发生的事。

normal.en: The rope strained under the weight.
normal.cn: 绳子在重物下绷得紧紧的。

normal.en: She strained to hear him.
He strained his back lifting the box.
The long journey put a strain on them.
normal.cn: 长途旅行给他们造成了压力。

normal.en: The bridge is under strain.

abstract.en: A strained rope sings the loudest.
abstract.cn: 绷紧的绳子，唱得最响。

abstract.en: Some things break precisely because they held too long.
abstract.cn: 有些东西之所以断裂，正因为撑得太久。

abstract.en: Strain shows where the strength ends.
abstract.cn: 压力，标出了力量的边界。

examples.en: The rope strained under the weight.
examples.cn: 绳子在重物下绷得紧紧的。

examples.en: She strained to hear him.
examples.cn: 她使劲去听他说的话。

examples.en: The strain of the journey tired them.
examples.cn: 旅途的劳累让他们疲惫。

dict_mnemonic.text: strain 是「拉紧」，也指「尽力」「扭伤」和「压力」；strain a muscle 是拉伤肌肉，under strain 是处于压力下，put a strain on 是给某事造成压力。

root: 经古法语 estraindre 来自拉丁语 stringere（拉紧、束紧）；由绷紧绳索的物理动作，引申为用力、拉伤肌肉，再引申为精神与生活上的压力。

sensesIntro.en: Strain is to pull tight, to try hard, to injure a muscle, or pressure and worry.
sensesIntro.cn: strain 是拉紧、尽力、扭伤肌肉，或压力与忧虑。

core.en: A rope pulled past its comfort.
core.cn: 一根被拉过舒适限度的绳子。

branches.en: The rope strained under the weight.
branches.cn: 绳子在重物下绷得紧紧的。

branches.en: She strained to hear him.
branches.cn: 她使劲去听他说的话。

branches.en: He strained his back.
branches.cn: 他拉伤了背。

branches.en: The strain of the journey tired them.
branches.cn: 旅途的劳累让他们疲惫。

branches.en: A tight rope and a tired mind feel the same pull.
branches.cn: 绷紧的绳与疲惫的心，承受着同一种拉力。

intro.en: Strain takes endings and builds words for pressure.
intro.cn: strain 加词尾，构成与压力相关的词。

latinIntro.en: The Latin source stringere meant to draw tight.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语来源 stringere 意为拉紧。

items.example: The dog was straining at the leash.
Pour the tea through a strainer.

items.meaning: to try as hard as possible
items.example: They strained every nerve to win.

definition_zh: 海峡；水道；困境；狭窄的；严格的
definition_en: a narrow passage of water between two larger bodies of water, or a difficult situation
core_image: 两片陆地之间一条狭窄的水道，船只能一艘接一艘通过
scene: 渡船每小时穿过一次海峡。Ferries cross the strait every hour.
sceneCN: 这里该词指「连接两片海域的狭窄水道」（第 1 个义项：海峡）；句意为渡船每小时穿过一次海峡。

pos.zh: 狭窄的；严格的（现多用于固定搭配）

senses.title: A narrow sea passage
senses.titleCN: 海峡：两片陆地间的狭窄水道
senses.definition: a narrow passage of water joining two larger bodies of water
senses.definitionCN: 连接两片较大海域的狭窄水道
senses.example: Ferries cross the strait every hour.
senses.exampleCN: 渡船每小时穿过一次海峡。
senses.why: The word first meant 'narrow' or 'tight', and a narrow passage of sea is simply that narrowness applied to water.
senses.whyCN: 这个词最初意为「狭窄、紧绷」，而狭窄的海上通道就是把「窄」用到水上。

senses.title: The waters of such a passage
senses.definition: the water area within a narrow passage, used for navigation
senses.definitionCN: 狭窄通道内的水域，供航行使用
senses.example: Currents in the strait run faster than in the open sea.
senses.exampleCN: 海峡里的水流比外海更快。
senses.why: The passage is also a place, so the word names the water inside it as well as the route.
senses.whyCN: 通道也是地点，因此这个词既指路线，也指其中的水域。

senses.title: A difficult situation
senses.definition: a difficult or dangerous situation, usually in the plural
senses.definitionCN: 困难或危险的处境，通常用复数
senses.example: The company is in dire straits after the flood.
senses.exampleCN: 洪水之后公司陷入严重困境。
senses.why: A narrow passage offers little room to move, so the plural became a picture of a pressing situation.
senses.whyCN: 狭窄通道几乎没有回旋余地，复数形式便成为紧迫处境的图景。

senses.title: Narrow or tight
senses.definition: narrow, tight or confined, an older adjective use
senses.definitionCN: 狭窄、紧绷或受限制的，较旧的形容词用法
senses.example: They passed through a strait gate into the yard.
senses.exampleCN: 他们穿过一道窄门进入院子。
senses.why: This is the original sense of the Latin root, kept in older and biblical style.
senses.whyCN: 这是拉丁词根的原义，保留在较旧与圣经风格的语言中。

senses.title: Strict in behaviour
senses.definition: strict or morally narrow, especially in the fixed phrase strait-laced
senses.definitionCN: 严格或道德上狭隘的，尤用于固定短语
senses.example: His strait-laced upbringing made him avoid any joke about money.
senses.exampleCN: 他拘谨的教养使他不肯拿钱开玩笑。
senses.why: Moral narrowness is a tightness of behaviour, so the old adjective survives in this phrase.
senses.whyCN: 道德上的狭隘就是行为上的紧绷，旧形容词因此留在这个短语里。

senses.title: Short of money
senses.definition: limited in money or resources, in the phrase straitened circumstances
senses.definitionCN: 钱财或资源受限，用于「拮据的境况」这一说法
senses.example: The family lived in straitened circumstances for years.
senses.exampleCN: 这家人多年生活拮据。
senses.why: Being pressed for money is being squeezed into a narrow space, which is the root image again.
senses.whyCN: 缺钱就是被挤进狭窄空间，又回到词根的意象。

senses.title: A narrow anatomical passage
senses.titleCN: 解剖或地理中的狭窄通道
senses.definition: a narrow passage in the body or in a landscape
senses.definitionCN: 身体或地形中的狭窄通道
senses.example: The pelvic strait is the narrowest part of the birth canal.
senses.exampleCN: 骨盆峡是产道最窄的部分。
senses.why: The narrow-passage sense extends from sea to any confined channel.
senses.whyCN: 狭窄通道义从海上扩展到任何受限制的通道。

senses.title: A proper name for a sea passage
senses.definition: a capitalized name for a particular sea passage, as in the Straits of Dover
senses.definitionCN: 某一特定海上通道的专名，如多佛海峡
senses.example: Ships wait for the tide before entering the Straits.
senses.exampleCN: 船只在进入海峡前等待潮水。
senses.why: Named passages become proper nouns, and the plural form is conventional for some of them.
senses.whyCN: 被命名的通道成为专名，其中一些惯用复数形式。

intro.en: Strait comes from Latin strictus 'drawn tight', through Old French estreit 'narrow'. The same root gives strict and stringent. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: 该词来自拉丁语表示「拉紧的」分词，经古法语「狭窄的」进入英语。同一词根还给出表示严格与严厉的词。年代均为约数。

items.en: stringere meant 'to draw tight, bind, compress', and it also gives English strain and stringent.
items.cn: 拉丁语词意为「拉紧、束缚、压缩」，也给出英语中表示拉紧与严厉的词。

items.en: The participle strictus 'drawn tight, narrow' became the adjective behind the English word.
items.cn: 分词形式意为「被拉紧的、狭窄的」，成为英语词背后的形容词。

items.en: Old French estreit meant 'tight, narrow, close', and English borrowed it in the Middle Ages.
items.cn: 古法语词意为「紧绷、狭窄、贴近」，英语在中世纪借入。

items.en: The geographic sense narrows the adjective to a narrow sea passage between two lands.
items.cn: 地理义把形容词收窄为两片陆地之间的狭窄海上通道。

items.en: The plural straits shifted from narrow water to a narrow, pressing situation, hence dire straits.
items.cn: 复数形式从狭窄水域转为狭窄紧迫的处境，因此有「严重困境」之说。

items.en: Source uncertain (first date): the earliest English citation is approximate, and the adjective is now archaic outside fixed phrases.
items.cn: 来源不确定（首见年代）：英语最早书证为约数，形容词除固定短语外已属古旧。

note.en: Group one holds look-alike words, including a famous false pair; group two holds the water terms that overlap with a strait.
note.cn: 第一组是形近词，其中有一对著名的假同源；第二组是与海峡语义重叠的水域词。

entries.definition: Direct, not curved or bent; it comes from a different Old English root meaning 'stretched', so it is a false relative.
entries.definitionCN: 指直的、不弯的；来自另一个意为「伸展」的古英语词根，因此是假同源。

entries.definition: Severe or exact, from the same Latin participle 'drawn tight'; it describes rules, not water.
entries.definitionCN: 指严厉或精确的，同出表示「拉紧」的拉丁分词；它描述规则，不描述水。

entries.definition: Strict and binding, from the same tightening root; it is used of laws and tests.
entries.definitionCN: 指严格而有约束力的，同出「拉紧」词根；用于法律与检验。

entries.definition: To stretch or press tightly, or the pressure itself; it shares the tightening image but not the geography.
entries.definitionCN: 指拉紧或挤压，或指这种压力；共享「拉紧」意象，但不用于地理。

entries.definition: A water passage, often a deeper route for ships; it is wider in use than a strait.
entries.definitionCN: 指水上通道，常为供船行的较深路线；使用范围比海峡更广。

entries.definition: A narrow sea passage, especially between an island and the mainland; it is close to strait but more local.
entries.definitionCN: 指狭窄的海上通道，尤指岛与大陆之间；与海峡接近，但更具地方性。

entries.definition: Any way through, by water or land; it is the general term that strait narrows.
entries.definitionCN: 指任何通过之路，水陆皆可；它是海峡所收窄的通用词。

entries.definition: A large area of sea partly enclosed by land; it is broad, while a strait is narrow.
entries.definitionCN: 指部分被陆地围住的大片海域；它宽阔，而海峡狭窄。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real collocations and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: The root means 'drawn tight', and a strait is water drawn into a narrow passage.
normal.cn: 词根意为「拉紧」，海峡就是被拉成狭窄通道的水。

normal.en: The family runs strait, straits, straitened, strait-laced and straitjacket.
normal.cn: 同族词包括本词、困境复数、拮据形容词、拘谨形容词与拘束衣。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the senses: the Strait of Gibraltar, dire straits, strait-laced.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出各义项：直布罗陀海峡、严重困境、拘谨的。

normal.en: Do not confuse it with the word for 'direct', which looks the same and comes from a different root.
normal.cn: 不要把它与表示「直的」那一个词混淆，二者同形却词根不同。

normal.en: A strait is water between lands, the opposite of an isthmus, which is land between waters.
normal.cn: 海峡是陆地之间的水，与地峡相反，后者是水之间的陆地。

abstract.en: Picture a tight collar that leaves almost no room to turn the head.
abstract.cn: 想象一只紧领子，几乎不给人转头的余地。

abstract.en: Picture a narrow door between two large rooms, with people filing through.
abstract.cn: 想象两个大房间之间一道窄门，人们排队通过。

abstract.en: Picture a corridor whose walls press closer with every step.
abstract.cn: 想象一条走廊，每走一步两壁就更紧。

examples.en: The strait is too shallow for the largest ships.
examples.cn: 这道海峡对最大的船来说太浅。

examples.en: After the factory closed, the town was in dire straits.
examples.cn: 工厂关闭后，小镇陷入严重困境。

examples.en: A lighthouse marks the narrowest point of the strait.
examples.cn: 一座灯塔标出海峡最窄处。

dict_mnemonic.text: 谐音「死追特」：船在窄海峡里只能死追着前船走。

root: 拉丁语 stringere「拉紧、束缚」的分词 strictus「拉紧的、狭窄的」，经古法语 estreit「狭窄的」进入英语；同一词根还构成 strict 与 stringent。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one tightness: water squeezed between two lands. The tightness then widens into the waters themselves, presses into a difficult situation, returns as an old adjective for narrow, becomes moral tightness, money shortage, an anatomical passage and a proper name.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项沿同一种「紧」展开：被两片陆地夹紧的水。这种紧随后扩展到水域本身、压成困境、回到表示狭窄的旧形容词、转为道德上的紧、钱财上的紧、解剖通道与专名。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: two shores pressing close together, leaving only a narrow lane of water.
core.cn: 核心意象：两岸紧紧靠拢，只留下一条狭窄的水道。

branches.en: THE PASSAGE: the narrow route, its water and its proper name are one place.
branches.cn: 通道：狭窄路线、其中的水与它的专名是同一个地方。

branches.en: TROUBLE: a passage with no room to move becomes a picture of hardship.
branches.cn: 困境：没有回旋余地的通道成为困苦的图景。

branches.en: TIGHTNESS OF RULE: narrow in space and strict in behaviour are the same root image.
branches.cn: 规则之紧：空间上的窄与行为上的严是同一词根意象。

branches.en: MONEY: being short is being squeezed into a narrow margin.
branches.cn: 钱财：短缺就是被挤进狭窄的余量。

branches.en: BODY: anatomy uses the same narrow-passage image.
branches.cn: 身体：解剖学使用同一狭窄通道意象。

intro.en: Strait is a Latin participle turned English noun, and the tightening root builds a small but common family.
intro.cn: 该词是拉丁分词转成的英语名词，其「拉紧」词根构成一个小而常见的词族。

latinIntro.en: Latin stringere and strictus give strait, strict, stringent and strain; the prefixes and endings decide the shade.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语的「拉紧」动词与分词给出本词以及表示严格、严厉与拉紧的词；前缀与词尾决定意味。

items.example: The root supplies the image of tightening.
items.exampleCN: 这个词根提供「收紧」的意象。

items.example: The participle became the adjective behind the noun.
items.exampleCN: 这个分词成为名词背后的形容词。

items.example: Ferries cross the strait every hour.
The town is in dire straits.
His strait-laced aunt disapproved of the plan.
items.exampleCN: 他古板的姑妈不赞成这个计划。

items.example: The rules became a straitjacket for the staff.
items.exampleCN: 这些规定成了员工的束缚。

items.example: The school has strict rules about lateness.
items.exampleCN: 学校对迟到有严格规定。

items.example: Stringent tests protect the water supply.

definition_en: a narrow band used to fasten or carry something, or to fasten something with such a band
core_image: 一条绕过箱子、被扣紧的宽皮带
scene: 他用一条皮带把箱子绑紧。He tightened the strap around the box.
sceneCN: 这里 strap 是「带子」（第 1 个义项）；句意：他用一条皮带把箱子绑紧。

senses.title: A fastening band
senses.definition: a narrow band used to fasten or carry something
senses.definitionCN: 用来捆扎或承提物品的窄带
senses.example: He tightened the strap around the box.
senses.exampleCN: 他把箱子上的带子勒紧。
senses.why: This is the basic object sense.
senses.whyCN: 这是最基本的实物义项。

senses.title: A worn band
senses.definition: a band worn over the shoulder or around the wrist
senses.definitionCN: 挂在肩上或绕在腕上的带子
senses.example: Her shoulder strap slipped.
senses.exampleCN: 她的肩带滑了下来。
senses.why: The same band is worn rather than tied.
senses.whyCN: 同一类带子从捆扎变成了穿戴。

senses.title: Fasten with a strap
senses.definition: to fasten something with a strap
senses.definitionCN: 用带子把某物固定住
senses.example: Strap the bag to the bike.
senses.exampleCN: 把包绑在自行车上。
senses.why: The noun turns into the action it allows.
senses.whyCN: 名词转化为它所带来的动作。

intro.en: Strap travelled from Greek through Latin and French.
intro.cn: strap 从希腊语经拉丁语与法语传入英语。

items.en: Strophos meant a twisted band.
items.cn: strophos 指扭成的带子。

items.en: Stroppus meant a thong.
items.cn: stroppus 指皮条。

items.en: Estrop meant a loop or band.
items.cn: estrop 指环或带。

items.en: Strap named a narrow band.
items.cn: strap 指窄带。

items.en: Strap became a verb for fastening.
items.cn: strap 成为表示捆扎的动词。

note.en: Strap is compared with look-alike words and with words for bands and belts.
note.cn: 把 strap 与形近词以及表示带子和皮带的词作比较。

entries.definition: a band worn around the waist

normalIntro.en: A strap holds things together so they can travel.
normalIntro.cn: strap 把东西绑在一起，好让它们上路。

normal.en: He tightened the strap around the box.
normal.cn: 他把箱子上的带子勒紧。

normal.en: Strap the bag to the bike.
Her shoulder strap slipped.
The watch strap is worn.
Strap in before we start.

abstract.en: A strap is a promise that nothing will be dropped.
abstract.cn: 带子，是一个不让东西掉下去的承诺。

abstract.en: What is strapped down can still be carried far.
abstract.cn: 绑稳的东西，才能被带到很远。

abstract.en: Some burdens are lightened by a good strap.
abstract.cn: 有些重担，会被一条好带子分担。

examples.en: He tightened the strap around the box.
examples.cn: 他把箱子上的带子勒紧。

examples.en: Strap the bag to the bike.
examples.cn: 把包绑在自行车上。

examples.en: Her shoulder strap slipped.

definition_zh: 分层；层理；社会分层；温度或密度分层；种子层积处理
definition_en: the arrangement of material, people or data in distinct layers, or the process that produces such layers
core_image: 一段被切开的土坡，深浅相间的薄层像被压紧的书页
scene: 老湖床被采砂场切开，深浅交替的薄层像压紧的书页，学生用尺量每一层的厚度。 Each color band records a year of stratification in the old lake bed.
sceneCN: 这里 stratification 指「沉积物按时间层层叠积形成层理的过程与结果」（第 1 个义项：地质上物质分层排列）；句意为每一道色带都记录了老湖床中一年的分层沉积。图中可辨识物件：采砂切面、深浅色带、卷尺、记录本。

pos.zh: 分层；层理；分层作用；社会阶层化；层积处理

senses.title: Rock arranged in layers
senses.titleCN: 岩石按层排列形成的层理
senses.definition: the layering of sedimentary rock, in which each bed records a separate episode of deposition
senses.definitionCN: 沉积岩成层排列，每一层记录一次独立的沉积事件
senses.example: Stratification in the cliff is so regular that each bed can be traced for a mile.
senses.exampleCN: 崖壁上的层理十分规整，每一层都能追踪一英里远。
senses.why: the suffix -fication marks a making or forming, so the noun names both the layered result and the process that produced it.
senses.whyCN: 后缀 -fication 表示「使形成」，因此名词同时指分层的结果与造成它的过程。

senses.title: Social ranking into strata
senses.definition: the division of a society into ranked groups distinguished by wealth, occupation or status
senses.definitionCN: 社会按财富、职业或地位划分为有高低之别的群体
senses.example: Studies of stratification ask why birth still predicts income so strongly.
senses.exampleCN: 分层研究追问：为何出身仍能如此强烈地预测收入。
senses.why: sociology borrowed the geological image deliberately: layers lie one above another, and the lower ones are hard to climb out of.
senses.whyCN: 社会学有意借用地质意象：层一层压一层，下面的层难以爬出。

senses.title: The act of layering
senses.definition: the process by which material becomes arranged in layers, whether by settling, sorting or design
senses.definitionCN: 物质因沉降、分选或人为设计而排列成层的过程
senses.example: Stratification began as soon as the current slowed and the coarse grains dropped out.
senses.exampleCN: 流速一慢、粗颗粒落下，分层就开始了。
senses.why: as a process noun it answers how, not what: the emphasis falls on the sorting that separates one layer from the next.
senses.whyCN: 作为过程名词它回答「如何」而非「什么」，重点在把一层与下一层分开的分选作用。

senses.title: Thermal or density layering
senses.titleCN: 温度或密度造成的分层
senses.definition: the separation of a body of water or air into layers that mix little because of temperature or salinity differences
senses.definitionCN: 水体或大气因温度或盐度差异分成几乎不混合的层
senses.example: Thermal stratification keeps the cold deep water cut off from the surface in summer.
senses.exampleCN: 夏季的温度分层使深层冷水与表层水隔开。
senses.why: physics uses the same noun because the water genuinely forms sheets that resist mixing, like beds of sediment.
senses.whyCN: 物理学沿用同一名词，因为水体真的形成抗拒混合的水片，像沉积层一样。

senses.title: Cold treatment of seeds
senses.titleCN: 种子层积处理（低温层积）
senses.definition: the practice of keeping moist seed at low temperature so that dormancy is broken and germination can start
senses.definitionCN: 把湿润种子置于低温以打破休眠、促成发芽的处理
senses.example: The growers use stratification to bring apple seed out of dormancy.
senses.exampleCN: 种植者用层积处理打破苹果种子的休眠。
senses.why: the older horticultural technique really did stack seed between layers of sand, so the name is literal before it is technical.
senses.whyCN: 较早的园艺做法确实把种子夹在沙层之间，因此这个名称先是字面义，后成技术术语。

senses.title: Layering of vegetation
senses.definition: the vertical division of a plant community into canopy, shrub, herb and ground layers
senses.definitionCN: 植物群落按冠层、灌木层、草本层与地被层在垂直方向分层
senses.example: Stratification in the rainforest decides which seedlings get any light at all.
senses.exampleCN: 雨林中的成层结构决定了哪些幼苗能见到光。
senses.why: ecology extended the noun from rock to living cover, where each layer intercepts light before it reaches the next.
senses.whyCN: 生态学把这个名词从岩石扩展到活植被：每层都在下一层之前截住光。

senses.title: Stratified sampling
senses.definition: the statistical practice of dividing a population into subgroups before sampling, so that each group is fairly represented
senses.definitionCN: 抽样前先把总体分成若干子群，使各组都得到公平代表
senses.example: Stratification by district made the survey's margins of error much smaller.
senses.exampleCN: 按地区分层使这项调查的误差范围小了很多。
senses.why: statistics took the noun for a designed layering, where the strata are chosen by the researcher rather than deposited by nature.
senses.whyCN: 统计学借这个名词指人为设计的层，其层由研究者选定，而非自然沉积。

senses.title: Archaeological layering
senses.definition: the sequence of occupation layers at a site, in which the lowest deposits are normally the oldest
senses.definitionCN: 遗址中居住层的叠压序列，通常最下的堆积最早
senses.example: Stratification at the site was undisturbed, so the pottery sequence could be read plainly.
senses.exampleCN: 遗址的地层未被扰动，陶器序列因此可以清楚读出。
senses.why: archaeology depends on the geological rule that layers stack in order, which makes depth a clock.
senses.whyCN: 考古学依赖地质学那条规则：层按顺序叠压，于是深度成了钟表。

intro.en: Stratification joins Latin stratum 'a layer, something spread out' to -fication, from facere 'to make'. It was formed in modern scientific Latin and passed into English in the eighteenth century. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: stratification 由拉丁 stratum「层、铺开之物」加 -fication（源自 facere「做」）构成，形成于近代科学拉丁语，十八世纪进入英语。年代均为约数。

items.en: Stratum is the neuter past participle of sternere 'to spread out, stretch, lay flat', so a stratum is literally something spread down.
items.cn: stratum 是 sternere「铺开、伸展、平放」的中性过去分词，因此 stratum 字面上就是「被铺下的东西」。

items.en: Roman writers used stratum for a bed, a couch or a paved surface; the geological sense of a rock bed is a later scientific narrowing.
items.cn: 罗马作家用 stratum 指床、卧榻或铺过的地面；指岩层的地质义是后来的科学收窄。

items.en: Scientists of the eighteenth century joined stratum to -fication, modelled on other technical nouns in -ficatio, to name the making of layers.
items.cn: 十八世纪学者仿照其它以 -ficatio 结尾的技术名词，把 stratum 与 -fication 结合，命名「成层」这一过程。

items.en: The noun became standard for sedimentary bedding, and stratigraphy grew up around the rule that layers are stacked in time order.
items.cn: 这个名词成为沉积层理的标准术语，地层学围绕「层按时间顺序叠压」这一规则发展起来。

items.en: From the nineteenth century the word was applied to ranked social groups, and later to deliberately divided sampling groups.
items.cn: 从十九世纪起，这个词被用于有高低之别的社会群体，后来又用于有意划分的抽样组。

items.en: Source uncertain (first dating only): the Latin elements are secure, but the earliest English use of the scientific noun is dated only approximately.
items.cn: 来源不确定（仅首见年代）：拉丁成分是确定的，但这个科学名词在英语中的最早使用只能约略定年。

note.en: Group one sets stratification against look-alikes built on other roots; group two sets it against words for layers and ranking.
note.cn: 第一组把 stratification 与其它词根构成的形近词分开；第二组区分它与「层」「等级」的其它说法。

entries.definition: The single layer itself; stratification is the arrangement or the process that produces many strata.
entries.definitionCN: 指单个层本身；stratification 指多层排列或其形成过程。

entries.definition: The Latin plural of stratum, used in English for several layers; it names the objects, not the process.
entries.definitionCN: stratum 的拉丁复数，英语中指若干层；它命名对象，不命名过程。

entries.definition: The verb 'to make or become layered'; the noun is its action and result.
entries.definitionCN: 动词「使成层、分层」；名词是其动作与结果。

entries.definition: From Greek stratēgos 'general', built on stratos 'army' and agein 'to lead'; the strat- overlap is accidental.
entries.definitionCN: 来自希腊 stratēgos「将军」，由 stratos「军队」与 agein「引导」构成；strat- 的重合只是偶然。

entries.definition: The everyday word for putting things in layers; stratification is its technical and geological counterpart.
entries.definitionCN: 指把东西分成层的日常词；stratification 是其技术与地质上的对应词。

entries.definition: The appearance of distinct stripes of colour or texture, which may result from stratification but need not.
entries.definitionCN: 指颜色或质地呈明显条带的外观，可由分层造成，但不必然。

entries.definition: A system of ranked levels, especially in organizations; it stresses order and authority rather than layers of material.
entries.definitionCN: 指按等级排列的体系，尤用于组织；强调次序与权力，而非物质的层。

entries.definition: Any splitting into parts; it says nothing about whether the parts lie one above another.
entries.definitionCN: 泛指分成若干部分，不说明这些部分是否上下叠压。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real collocations and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: stratum 'layer' + -fication 'making': the making of layers.
The same stratum stock gives stratum, strata, stratify, stratified, stratigraphy.
normal.cn: 同一 stratum 词干衍生 stratum、strata、stratify、stratified、stratigraphy。

normal.en: Geology reads layers; sociology reads ranks; statistics reads subgroups; horticulture reads cold sand.
normal.cn: 地质读层，社会学读等级，统计学读子群，园艺读冷沙。

normal.en: Fixed phrases: social stratification, thermal stratification, seed stratification.
normal.cn: 固定搭配：社会分层、温度分层、种子层积处理。

normal.en: Keep it apart from strategy, whose strat- comes from Greek stratos 'army'.
normal.cn: 与 strategy 分开，后者的 strat- 来自希腊 stratos「军队」。

abstract.en: Picture a cake cut cleanly so that every sponge line shows.
abstract.cn: 想象蛋糕被切开，每一道蛋糕坯的层次都露出来。

abstract.en: Picture a lake in summer with a warm lid that will not mix with the cold below.
abstract.cn: 想象夏日的湖，上面一层温水盖着，不肯与下面的冷水混合。

abstract.en: Picture a library where every shelf is a social class and the ladder is missing.
abstract.cn: 想象一座图书馆，每层书架是一个社会阶层，而梯子不见了。

examples.en: The stratification of the delta records centuries of floods.
examples.cn: 三角洲的层理记录了数百年的洪水。

examples.en: Educational stratification widened even as enrolments rose.
examples.cn: 入学人数上升的同时，教育分层反而加剧。

examples.en: Without stratification, the lake bottom would lose its oxygen each summer.
examples.cn: 若没有温度分层，湖底每年夏天都会缺氧。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「strata（层）+ fication（做成）」——把东西做成一层层 → 分层

root: 拉丁 stratum「层、铺开之物」（sternere 的过去分词）+ -fication（facere「做」），近代科学拉丁语构词。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses all turn on stacked layers: first rock, then society, then the act, then water, seed, forest and data, until depth itself becomes a clock.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项都围绕「层层叠压」：先是岩石，再是社会，再是动作本身，然后是水、种子、森林与数据，最后深度本身成了钟表。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a cut bank showing band after band, each band a year.
core.cn: 核心意象：被切开的土坡露出一条条色带，每一带是一年。

branches.en: ROCK AND ITS MAKING: the same noun covers the beds and the process that lays them.
branches.cn: 岩石与其形成：同一名词兼指层与被层铺出的过程。

branches.en: SOCIAL LAYERS: geology supplies the image of ranks that are hard to climb.
branches.cn: 社会层：地质提供了难以攀爬的等级意象。

branches.en: WATER LAYERS: density builds real sheets that refuse to mix.
branches.cn: 水层：密度造出真的、拒绝混合的水片。

branches.en: SEED AND FOREST: cold sand and canopy light both create usable layers.
branches.cn: 种子与森林：冷沙与冠层的光都在造可用之层。

branches.en: DESIGNED STRATA: sampling groups and occupation layers both read the past from below.
branches.cn: 有意划分的层：抽样组与居住层都从下面读取过去。

intro.en: Stratification is a modern Latin compound whose two parts still work separately in English, so the whole word can be read as layer plus making.
intro.cn: stratification 是近代拉丁复合词，两个部分在英语中仍独立运作，因此整词可读作「层」加「做成」。

latinIntro.en: Latin stratum 'layer' and the suffix -fication from facere 'to make' supply the meaning; stratum itself comes from sternere 'to spread out'.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 stratum「层」与源自 facere「做」的后缀 -fication 提供词义；stratum 本身来自 sternere「铺开」。

items.example: Winds stratify the ash by grain size.

senses.title: A single rock layer

senses.exampleCN: 这里的石灰岩层还不到一米厚。
senses.why: the Latin word means something spread out, so a stratum is one sheet laid over another rather than a mass.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁词义是「铺开之物」，因此 stratum 是铺在另一层上的一层薄片，而非一大块体。

senses.title: A social class layer
senses.definition: one of the ranked groups into which a society is divided by wealth, occupation or status
senses.definitionCN: 社会按财富、职业或地位划分出的有高低之别的群体之一
senses.example: Families from every stratum of the town came to the funeral.
senses.exampleCN: 镇上各个阶层的家庭都来参加葬礼。
senses.why: sociology keeps the geological metaphor singular: one stratum among many, each resting on the one below.
senses.whyCN: 社会学保留地质比喻的单数形式：众多层中的一层，各自压在下一层之上。

senses.title: Any thin sheet of material
senses.definition: a thin continuous sheet of one substance lying over another, as of paint, dust or tissue
senses.definitionCN: 一种物质覆盖在另一种之上的连续薄层，如漆、尘或组织
senses.example: A stratum of ash from the eruption still lies over the fields.
senses.exampleCN: 火山喷发留下的火山灰层仍覆盖着田野。
senses.why: the word is general enough to leave geology: any flat sheet counts, provided it lies on something else.
senses.whyCN: 这个词足够一般，可以离开地质：只要铺在别物之上，任何平层都算。

senses.title: An anatomical layer
senses.definition: one of the distinct layers of a tissue or organ, such as the outer horny layer of skin
senses.definitionCN: 组织或器官中可区分的一层，如皮肤最外的角质层
senses.example: The outermost stratum of the skin consists of dead flattened cells.
senses.exampleCN: 皮肤最外层由扁平的死细胞构成。
senses.why: anatomy borrowed the noun because skin and gut really are built of sheets that peel apart.
senses.whyCN: 解剖学借这个名词，因为皮肤与肠壁确实由可分离的片层构成。

senses.title: An occupation layer on a site
senses.definition: a distinct band of debris and structures left by one period of human use at an archaeological site
senses.definitionCN: 考古遗址中某一时期人类活动留下的、含遗物与结构的独立堆积带
senses.example: The earliest stratum yielded only flint flakes and no pottery.
senses.exampleCN: 最早的居住层只出燧石片，没有陶器。
senses.why: archaeology treats each stratum as a sealed episode, so mixing between strata destroys the chronology.
senses.whyCN: 考古学把每一层视为封闭的一段，因此层间混扰会毁掉年代序列。

senses.title: A layer of the atmosphere or sea
senses.definition: a horizontal band of air or water distinguished by temperature, salt content or composition
senses.definitionCN: 按温度、盐度或成分区分出的空气或水的水平带
senses.example: Ozone forms in a high stratum of the atmosphere and drifts downward.
senses.exampleCN: 臭氧在对流层之上的高空中形成，并向下飘移。
senses.why: meteorology uses stratum for bands that behave as units, just as sedimentary beds do.
senses.whyCN: 气象学用 stratum 指作为整体运动的气带，正如沉积层那样。

senses.title: One level of a system
senses.definition: one level of an organized system, such as a language, a legal code or an administrative structure
senses.definitionCN: 有组织体系中的一层，如语言、法典或行政结构中的层级
senses.example: Archaic spellings survived in the lowest stratum of the written language.
senses.exampleCN: 古旧拼写残留在书面语言的最底层。
senses.why: the abstract use generalizes the image: levels rest on levels, and the deepest ones are the oldest and least visible.
senses.whyCN: 抽象义把意象一般化：层层叠压，最深者最古老、最不易见。

senses.title: A sampling subgroup
senses.definition: one of the subgroups into which a population is divided before a sample is drawn
senses.definitionCN: 抽样之前把总体划分成的子群之一
senses.example: Each stratum was sampled separately so that small districts were not lost.
senses.exampleCN: 每一层都单独抽样，以免小区被淹没。
senses.why: statistics makes the layer a deliberate construction, chosen so that variation inside it stays small.
senses.whyCN: 统计学把层变成有意的构造，选择的依据是层内差异要小。

intro.en: Stratum is Latin for 'something spread out', the neuter past participle of sternere 'to spread, lay flat'. English adopted it in the sixteenth century, first for beds of rock. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: stratum 是拉丁语「铺开之物」，为 sternere「铺开、平放」的中性过去分词。英语于十六世纪引入，最初指岩层。年代均为约数。

items.en: Sternere meant 'to spread out, stretch, lay flat'; its participle stratus gave Latin stratum, a thing spread down.
items.cn: 一般认为 sternere 意为「铺开、伸展、平放」；其分词 stratus 产生拉丁 stratum，即被铺下之物。

items.en: In Latin, stratum covered a bed, a couch, a paved floor and a horse's saddle cloth, all surfaces laid over something.
items.cn: 在拉丁语中，stratum 指床、卧榻、铺过的地面与马鞍垫，都是铺在别物之上的面。

items.en: English naturalists of the sixteenth century took stratum for a bed of rock, and the plural strata followed with it.
items.cn: 十六世纪的英国博物学者用 stratum 指岩层，复数 strata 也随之进入英语。

items.en: Nineteenth-century social writers extended the noun to ranked classes, borrowing the image of layers stacked in order.
items.cn: 十九世纪的社会写作者把这个名词扩展到有等级的阶级，借用了层层叠压的意象。

items.en: Strata is the Latin plural and is often mistaken for a singular; the true singular remains stratum.
items.cn: strata 是拉丁复数，常被误当单数；真正的单数仍是 stratum。

items.en: Source uncertain (first dating only): the Latin etymon is secure, but the earliest English geological citation is dated only approximately.
items.cn: 来源不确定（仅首见年代）：拉丁词源是确定的，但英语中最早的地质学书证只能约略定年。

note.en: Group one marks the plural and derivative forms that are constantly mixed up with the singular; group two marks words for layers and levels that are not this noun.
note.cn: 第一组标出常与单数混淆的复数与派生形式；第二组标出并非本词却表「层」「级」的词。

entries.definition: The Latin plural: several layers at once. Writing 'a strata' is a common error, since the singular is stratum.
entries.definitionCN: 拉丁复数：一次指数层。写成 a strata 是常见错误，单数应为 stratum。

entries.definition: The arranging or forming of layers; it names the process, while stratum names one result.
entries.definitionCN: 分层的过程；它命名过程，stratum 命名其中一个结果。

entries.definition: To make or become layered; the noun does not itself carry an action.
entries.definitionCN: 使成层或成层；名词本身不含动作。

entries.definition: Greek stratēgos 'general' from stratos 'army'; it looks similar but has no connection with layers.
entries.definitionCN: 希腊 stratēgos「将军」，源自 stratos「军队」；形似但与层无关。

entries.definition: The plain term for one sheet over another, used of paint, dust, cake and rock alike.
entries.definitionCN: 指一层压一层的日常词，漆、尘、蛋糕与岩石都用它。

entries.definition: A geological layer thick enough to be mapped as a unit; a stratum may be thinner and less formal.
entries.definitionCN: 厚到可作为填图单位的地质层；stratum 可以更薄、更不正式。

entries.definition: A position in a scale or hierarchy, with no suggestion of physical sheeting.
entries.definitionCN: 指尺度或等级中的位置，不含实体薄片之意。

entries.definition: A thin band of coal or ore that can be mined; it implies economic use, which stratum does not.
entries.definitionCN: 可开采的薄煤层或矿带；含经济利用之意，stratum 则不含。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real collocations and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: Latin stratum is a thing spread out; the plural strata is often mistaken for a singular.
normal.cn: 拉丁 stratum 是铺开之物；复数 strata 常被误当单数。

normal.en: The family runs stratum, strata, stratal, stratify, stratification, substratum.
Geology says a bed, sociology says a class, anatomy says a sheet of skin.
normal.cn: 地质说岩层，社会学说阶层，解剖学说一层皮。

normal.en: Fixed phrases: rock stratum, upper stratum, stratum corneum.
normal.cn: 固定搭配：岩层、上层、角质层。

normal.en: Remember that -um is singular and -a is plural, as in datum and data.
normal.cn: 记住 -um 为单数、-a 为复数，如同 datum 与 data。

abstract.cn: 想象一栋楼，每层是一个阶层，楼梯有人把守。

examples.en: The stratum was sealed by lava and therefore undisturbed.
examples.cn: 该层被熔岩封住，因而未被扰动。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「strat（铺开）+ um（东西）」——铺开的一层东西 → 地层、阶层

root: 拉丁 stratum「铺开之物」，为 sternere「铺开、平放」的中性过去分词；复数 strata。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses all describe one sheet lying on another: rock first, then class, tissue, occupation debris, air, system level and sampling group.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项都描述「铺在另一层上的一层」：先是岩石，再是阶层、组织、居住堆积、空气、体系层级与抽样组。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a single sheet pressed into place between two others.
core.cn: 核心意象：一层薄片被压在另外两层之间。

branches.en: PHYSICAL SHEET: rock or ash, the point is that it is one continuous spread.
branches.cn: 实体薄层：岩石或火山灰，要点是它为一整片铺开之物。

branches.en: RANK AND LEVEL: layers of people and layers of systems obey the same up-down image.
branches.cn: 等级与层级：人的层与体系的层同守一个上下意象。

branches.en: BODY LAYER: skin and gut really do peel in sheets.
branches.cn: 身体层：皮肤与肠壁确实成片可剥。

branches.en: SEALED BANDS: occupation debris and atmospheric belts both behave as units.
branches.cn: 封闭的带：居住堆积与大气带都作为整体运作。

branches.en: CHOSEN LAYER: statistics builds its strata on purpose.
branches.cn: 选定的层：统计学的层是刻意划分的。

intro.en: Stratum is a bare Latin noun in English, but the same root builds a whole family through English and Latin affixes.
intro.cn: stratum 在英语中就是拉丁名词原形，但同一词根通过英语与拉丁词缀构成了整个词族。

latinIntro.en: Latin sternere 'to spread out' gives stratum and stratus; English adds -al, -ify, -ification and sub- to extend the family.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 sternere「铺开」产生 stratum 与 stratus；英语用 -al、-ify、-ification 与 sub- 扩展词族。

definition_en: to make something stronger, more solid, or more effective
core_image: 在一根柱子上再加一道支撑，让它更稳
scene: 锻炼能增强肌肉。Exercise can strengthen your muscles.
sceneCN: 这里 strengthen 是「增强」（第 1 个义项）；句意：锻炼能增强肌肉。

senses.title: Make physically stronger
senses.definition: to make a body, structure, or material stronger
senses.definitionCN: 使身体、结构或材料更强
senses.example: Exercise can strengthen your muscles.
senses.exampleCN: 锻炼能增强肌肉。
senses.why: This is added power in the body.
senses.whyCN: 这是给身体增加力量。

senses.title: Make a bond firmer
senses.definition: to make a relationship, position, or system more secure
senses.definitionCN: 使关系、地位或体系更稳固
senses.example: The visit strengthened ties between the two cities.
senses.exampleCN: 这次访问加强了两座城市之间的联系。
senses.why: Bonds can be braced like beams.
senses.whyCN: 关系也能像梁一样被加固。

senses.title: Make more convincing
senses.definition: to make an argument, feeling, or effect stronger
senses.definitionCN: 使论点、感受或效果更有力
senses.example: The new evidence strengthened her case.
senses.exampleCN: 新证据使她的论据更有力。
senses.why: A case stands like a structure and can be braced.
senses.whyCN: 论据像建筑一样立着，也能被加固。

intro.en: Strengthen is strength plus the verb ending -en.
intro.cn: strengthen 由 strength 加动词后缀 -en 构成。

items.en: Strengþu named power.
items.cn: strengþu 指力量。

items.en: Strengthen meant to give strength.
items.cn: 中古英语 strengthen 意为赋予力量。

items.en: It described making the body stronger.
items.cn: 它用来描写让身体更强壮。

items.en: It spread to buildings and systems.
items.cn: 词义扩展到建筑与制度。

items.en: It also came to mean making a case stronger.
items.cn: 也表示让论据更有力。

note.en: Strengthen is compared with look-alike words and with words for making stronger.
note.cn: 把 strengthen 与形近词以及表示加强的词作比较。

entries.definition: the measure from end to end

normalIntro.en: Strengthen is the act of adding strength to something already standing.
normalIntro.cn: strengthen 是给已经立着的东西再加一份力量。

normal.en: Walking strengthens the legs.
The two countries strengthened their ties.
A second lock strengthened the door.
The news strengthened her resolve.
normal.cn: 这个消息增强了她的决心。

normal.en: They strengthened the bridge with steel.
normal.cn: 他们用钢材加固了桥梁。

abstract.en: To strengthen is to help something hold its ground.
abstract.cn: 加强，就是帮某物站稳。

abstract.en: Bonds grow stronger by being used.
abstract.cn: 关系越用越牢固。

abstract.en: A brave choice strengthens the one who makes it.
abstract.cn: 勇敢的选择，会让做出选择的人更强。

examples.en: Exercise can strengthen your muscles.
examples.cn: 锻炼能增强肌肉。

examples.en: The visit strengthened ties between the two cities.
examples.cn: 这次访问加强了两座城市之间的联系。

examples.en: The new evidence strengthened her case.
examples.cn: 新证据使她的论据更有力。

dict_mnemonic.text: strengthen 是 strength 加 -en，也就是「使有力量」；肌肉变强是增强，关系变牢是巩固，论据变硬是更有力。

root: 由 strength（力量）加动词后缀 -en 构成；从给身体增加力量，扩展到加固结构与关系，再用于增强论据、信心与效果。

sensesIntro.en: Strengthen adds power to a body, firmness to a bond, and weight to an argument.
sensesIntro.cn: strengthen 给身体加力量，给关系加牢固，给论据加分量。

core.en: A second beam braced against the first.
core.cn: 第二根梁撑住第一根。

branches.en: A runner adds one more hill.
branches.cn: 跑者多跑一个坡。

branches.en: Two towns sign a new agreement.
branches.cn: 两座城镇签下新协议。

branches.en: A document supports the claim.
branches.cn: 一份文件支撑了主张。

branches.en: Practice strengthens both body and trust.
branches.cn: 练习既强身体，也强信任。

branches.en: Proof strengthens a promise between people.
branches.cn: 证据让人与人之间的承诺更稳。

intro.en: Strengthen takes verb endings and is built on strength.
intro.cn: strengthen 加动词词尾，其基础是 strength。

latinIntro.en: There is no Latin root; the word is Germanic.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词没有拉丁词根，属于日耳曼语来源。

items.meaning: to make a standing more secure
items.exampleCN: 这场胜利巩固了他的地位。

definition_en: worry caused by a difficult situation, special importance given to something, or the stronger sound in a word
core_image: 一根被拉紧的弦，绷得快要发出声音
scene: 考试前他感到很大压力。He felt a lot of stress before the exam.
sceneCN: 这里 stress 是「压力」（第 1 个义项）；句意：考试前他感到很大压力。

senses.title: Mental pressure
senses.definition: worry and tension caused by a difficult situation
senses.definitionCN: 困难处境造成的担忧与紧张
senses.example: He felt a lot of stress before the exam.
senses.exampleCN: 考试前他感到很大压力。
senses.why: This is pressure on the mind.
senses.whyCN: 这是压在心里的压力。

senses.title: Special emphasis
senses.definition: special importance given to something
senses.definitionCN: 给予某事物的特别重视
senses.example: The teacher stressed the need for rest.
senses.exampleCN: 老师强调了休息的必要。
senses.why: The mind presses on one point.
senses.whyCN: 心思在这里压住了一个重点。

senses.title: Strong sound
senses.definition: the stronger sound in a word or phrase
senses.definitionCN: 单词或短语中读得更强的音
senses.example: Put the stress on the first syllable.
senses.exampleCN: 把重音放在第一个音节上。
senses.why: Voice pressure marks the beat.
senses.whyCN: 声音的力度标出了节拍。

intro.en: Stress comes from distress, from Old French destrece, narrowness or hardship.
intro.cn: stress 由 distress 截短而来，源自法语 destrece，意为狭窄与艰难。

items.en: Strictus meant drawn tight.
items.cn: strictus 意为拉紧的。

items.en: Destrece named hardship and tightness.
items.cn: destrece 指艰难与紧绷。

items.en: Distresse named great trouble.
items.cn: 中古英语 distresse 指巨大的困苦。

items.en: Stress shortened the word and kept the pressure.
items.cn: stress 截短了词形，保留了压力之意。

items.en: It also named vocal emphasis.
items.cn: 它也开始指语音上的重音。

note.en: Stress is compared with look-alike words and with words for pressure.
note.cn: 把 stress 与形近词以及表示压力的词作比较。

entries.definition: force or worry pressing on someone

normalIntro.en: Stress is a tightened string, whether in the mind, the voice, or the sentence.
normalIntro.cn: stress 是一根绷紧的弦，可能在心里、在声音里，也可能在句子里。

normal.en: Too much stress harms sleep.
She stressed the value of teamwork.
normal.cn: 她强调了团队合作的价值。

normal.en: The word has stress on the second syllable.
normal.cn: 这个词的重音在第二个音节。

normal.en: He is under great stress at work.
normal.cn: 他工作时承受着巨大压力。

normal.en: Do not stress out over small things.

abstract.en: Stress is weight the mind puts on itself.
abstract.cn: 压力，是心给自己加的重量。

abstract.en: A stressed string can still make music.
abstract.cn: 绷紧的弦，依然能奏出音乐。

abstract.en: What we stress, we remember.
abstract.cn: 我们强调什么，就会记住什么。

examples.en: He felt a lot of stress before the exam.
examples.cn: 考试前他感到很大压力。

examples.en: The teacher stressed the need for rest.
examples.cn: 老师强调了休息的必要。

examples.en: Put the stress on the first syllable.
examples.cn: 把重音放在第一个音节上。

dict_mnemonic.text: stress 本义是「拉紧」；心里拉紧是压力，说话时把某点压重是强调，读音时把某个音节压重就是重音。

root: 源自拉丁语 strictus（拉紧），经法语 destrece 与中古英语 distresse 演变，截短为 stress；由紧绷与困苦，引申为心理压力、语义强调与语音重音。

sensesIntro.en: Stress is tension in the mind, weight on a point, and force in the voice.
sensesIntro.cn: stress 是心里的紧张、给某点的分量，以及声音里的力度。

core.en: A string pulled until it hums.
core.cn: 一根被拉到嗡嗡作响的弦。

branches.en: A student cannot sleep before the test.
branches.cn: 学生考前睡不着。

branches.en: A teacher repeats one key point.
branches.cn: 老师反复讲一个重点。

branches.en: One syllable sounds louder.
branches.cn: 一个音节读得更响。

branches.en: What we keep stressing becomes our worry.
branches.cn: 我们反复强调的东西，会变成忧虑。

branches.en: Emphasis in meaning lands as stress in sound.
branches.cn: 意思上的强调，落在声音上就是重音。

intro.en: Stress takes verb endings and builds adjective and noun forms.
intro.cn: stress 加动词词尾，并构成形容词与名词形式。

latinIntro.en: The Latin root is strictus, drawn tight.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁词根是 strictus，意为拉紧的。

items.example: The bank passed the stress test.
items.exampleCN: 这家银行通过了压力测试。

definition_en: to reach out your body, to spread over an area or time, or to pull something tight
core_image: 一个人双臂向上伸开，身体被拉得又长又直
scene: 她起床后伸了个懒腰。She stretched after getting out of bed.
sceneCN: 这里 stretch 是「伸展」（第 1 个义项）；句意：她起床后伸了个懒腰。

senses.title: Reach out the body
senses.definition: to extend your arms, legs, or body
senses.definitionCN: 伸开手臂、腿或身体
senses.example: She stretched after getting out of bed.
senses.exampleCN: 她起床后伸了个懒腰。
senses.why: This is the body making itself long.
senses.whyCN: 这是身体把自己拉长。

senses.title: Spread over an area
senses.definition: to continue over a distance or period
senses.definitionCN: 在空间或时间上延续
senses.example: The fields stretch for miles.
senses.exampleCN: 田野绵延数英里。
senses.why: The body's reach becomes the land's reach.
senses.whyCN: 身体的伸展变成了土地的伸展。

senses.title: Pull tight
senses.definition: to pull something so that it becomes tight or longer
senses.definitionCN: 把某物拉紧或拉长
senses.example: They stretched the rope across the river.
senses.exampleCN: 他们把绳子拉过河面。
senses.why: Here the pulling is done to an object.
senses.whyCN: 这个义项里，拉的动作落在物体上。

intro.en: Stretch comes from Old English streccan, to extend.
intro.cn: stretch 来自古英语 streccan，意为伸展。

items.en: Streccan meant to extend or reach out.
items.cn: streccan 意为伸展或伸出。

items.en: The root meant straight and stretched.
items.cn: 这个词根含有「直」与「拉长」之意。

items.en: Strecchen kept the sense of reaching.
items.cn: 中古英语 strecchen 仍指伸展。

items.en: Land and time could stretch too.
items.cn: 土地与时间也可以「延伸」。

items.en: At a stretch meant without a break.
items.cn: at a stretch 固定为连续不断之意。

note.en: Stretch is compared with look-alike words and with words for extending.
note.cn: 把 stretch 与形近词以及表示延伸的词作比较。

normalIntro.en: Stretch is length made on purpose, in a body, a road, or a rope.
normalIntro.cn: stretch 是刻意制造出来的长度，在身体、道路或绳子上都一样。

normal.en: Stretch your arms above your head.
The beach stretches along the coast.
We stopped to stretch our legs.
He stretched the rubber band.
She worked for hours at a stretch.
normal.cn: 她连续工作了好几个小时。

abstract.en: A stretch is a promise to become longer.
abstract.cn: 伸展，是一个变长的承诺。

abstract.en: Roads stretch because people need to arrive.
abstract.cn: 道路延伸，因为人需要抵达。

abstract.en: A stretched truth is thinner than it looks.
abstract.cn: 被拉长的事实，比看上去更薄。

examples.en: She stretched after getting out of bed.
examples.cn: 她起床后伸了个懒腰。

examples.en: The fields stretch for miles.
examples.cn: 田野绵延数英里。

examples.en: They stretched the rope across the river.
examples.cn: 他们把绳子拉过河面。

dict_mnemonic.text: stretch 的核心是「拉长」；身体拉长是伸展，土地拉长是延伸，绳子拉长是拉紧，说连续数小时就是 at a stretch。

root: 来自古英语 streccan（伸展、伸出），属日耳曼语词，与「直」的概念相关；由身体的伸展，扩展到空间与时间的绵延，再指把物体拉紧拉长。

sensesIntro.en: Stretch is a body reaching out, land or time continuing, or a rope pulled tight.
sensesIntro.cn: stretch 是身体伸出去、土地或时间延续下去，或绳子被拉紧。

core.en: Two arms opening wide above a waking body.
core.cn: 刚醒的身体上方张开两条手臂。

branches.en: A sleeper yawns and opens the arms.
branches.cn: 睡醒的人打着哈欠张开手臂。

branches.en: A road runs to the horizon.
branches.cn: 一条路一直伸到天边。

branches.en: A rope grows taut between two posts.
branches.cn: 绳子在两根柱子之间绷紧。

branches.en: The body learns length from the land.
branches.cn: 身体从土地那里学会了长度。

branches.en: Too much pulling can break what stretches.
branches.cn: 拉得太狠，会把伸展的东西拉断。

intro.en: Stretch takes verb endings and builds adjectives and nouns.
intro.cn: stretch 加动词词尾，并构成形容词与名词。

latinIntro.en: There is no Latin root; the word is Germanic.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词没有拉丁词根，属于日耳曼语来源。

items.meaning: a bed for carrying the sick
items.example: They carried him on a stretcher.
She stretched out on the sofa.
items.exampleCN: 她在沙发上伸展开身体。
我们去活动活动腿脚吧。

definition_en: to hit something, to stop work as a protest, or to come suddenly into the mind
core_image: 一只手挥下，击在目标上，发出清脆的响声
scene: 工人罢工要求提高工资。The workers went on strike for higher pay.
sceneCN: 这里 strike 是「罢工」（第 2 个义项）；句意：工人罢工要求提高工资。

senses.title: Hit
senses.definition: to hit someone or something with force
senses.definitionCN: 用力打某人或某物
senses.example: He struck the ball with his bat.
senses.exampleCN: 他用球棒击球。
senses.why: This is the physical blow.
senses.whyCN: 这是身体上的击打。

senses.title: Stop work
senses.definition: to stop working as a protest
senses.definitionCN: 为抗议而停止工作
senses.example: The workers went on strike for higher pay.
senses.exampleCN: 工人罢工要求提高工资。
senses.why: Workers strike against the employer.
senses.whyCN: 工人把行动「打」向雇主。

senses.title: Come to mind
senses.definition: to come suddenly into someone's mind
senses.definitionCN: 突然出现在某人脑海里
senses.example: A good idea struck me on the way home.
senses.exampleCN: 回家路上我忽然想到一个好主意。
senses.why: An idea lands like a blow.
senses.whyCN: 一个念头落下来，像一次击打。

senses.title: Attack suddenly
senses.definition: to attack or affect someone suddenly
senses.definitionCN: 突然袭击或影响某人
senses.example: The storm struck the coast at night.
senses.exampleCN: 暴风雨夜里袭击了海岸。
senses.why: Disaster arrives like a hit.
senses.whyCN: 灾害来临时，也像一次击打。

intro.en: Strike comes from Old English strican, to stroke or go.
intro.cn: strike 来自古英语 strican，意为抚摸或行走。

items.en: Strican meant to stroke or move.
items.cn: strican 意为抚摸或移动。

items.en: The root named a quick movement.
items.cn: 这个词根表示快速的动作。

items.en: Striken developed the sense of hitting.
items.cn: 中古英语 striken 发展出击打之意。

items.en: A strike became a workers' protest.
items.cn: strike 成为工人抗议的罢工。

items.en: Ideas and storms could strike too.
items.cn: 念头与风暴也可以「袭来」。

note.en: Strike is compared with look-alike words and with words for hitting.
note.cn: 把 strike 与形近词以及表示击打的词作比较。

normalIntro.en: Strike is a blow that can land on a ball, a job, a mind, or a coast.
normalIntro.cn: strike 这一击，可以落在球上、工作上、心里，也可以落在海岸上。

normal.en: He struck the drum twice.
The staff will strike on Monday.
A thought struck her suddenly.
The earthquake struck at dawn.
She struck a match in the dark.
normal.cn: 她在黑暗中划了根火柴。

abstract.en: A strike is a moment that insists on being felt.
abstract.cn: 一次击打，是非要被感觉到的一刻。

abstract.en: Ideas arrive like arrows from nowhere.
abstract.cn: 念头像不知从何而来的箭。

abstract.en: To stop work is also a kind of blow.
abstract.cn: 停下工作，也是一种击打。

examples.en: The workers went on strike for higher pay.
examples.cn: 工人罢工要求提高工资。

examples.en: He struck the ball with his bat.
examples.cn: 他用球棒击球。

examples.en: A good idea struck me on the way home.
examples.cn: 回家路上我忽然想到一个好主意。

dict_mnemonic.text: strike 本是一次「打」；工人用停工去打雇主就是罢工，念头打中你就是突然想到，风暴打来就是侵袭。

root: 来自古英语 strican（抚摸、移动），属日耳曼语词；由快速的动作发展出「击打」，再引申出罢工、突然想到与灾害侵袭。

sensesIntro.en: Strike is a blow, a work stoppage, a sudden idea, or a sudden attack.
sensesIntro.cn: strike 是一次击打、一场停工、一个突然的念头，或一次突然的侵袭。

core.en: A hand coming down on a target.
core.cn: 一只手朝目标落下。

branches.en: A bat meets a ball.
branches.cn: 球棒击中球。

branches.en: Workers leave the factory gate.
branches.cn: 工人走出厂门。

branches.en: An answer appears in the shower.
branches.cn: 答案在淋浴时冒出来。

branches.en: A storm reaches the shore.
branches.cn: 暴风雨抵达海岸。

branches.en: Both a strike and a storm interrupt the day.
branches.cn: 罢工与风暴都会打断日常。

intro.en: Strike takes irregular past forms and builds adjective and noun forms.
intro.cn: strike 有特殊过去式，并构成形容词与名词。

latinIntro.en: There is no Latin root; the word is Germanic.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词没有拉丁词根，属于日耳曼语来源。

items.meaning: one who strikes, or a forward

definition_en: thin cord used for tying, a series of similar things, or a cord that makes sound in an instrument
core_image: 一根细线从针眼穿过，把散落的东西串在一起
scene: 她用一根细绳把包裹捆好。She tied the parcel with a piece of string.
sceneCN: 这里 string 是「细绳」（第 1 个义项）；句意：她用一根细绳把包裹捆好。

senses.title: Thin cord
senses.definition: thin cord used to tie things
senses.definitionCN: 用来捆东西的细绳
senses.example: She tied the parcel with a piece of string.
senses.exampleCN: 她用一根细绳把包裹捆好。
senses.why: This is the cord in your hand.
senses.whyCN: 这是拿在手里的绳子。

senses.title: A series
senses.definition: a number of similar things in a line or series
senses.definitionCN: 排成一列或一连串的同类事物
senses.example: A string of lights hung across the street.
senses.exampleCN: 一串灯横挂在街道上方。
senses.why: Things on a cord become things in a row.
senses.whyCN: 串在绳上的东西，变成了一列。

senses.title: A musical cord
senses.definition: a tight cord on an instrument that makes sound
senses.definitionCN: 乐器上振动发声的绷紧的线
senses.example: One string of the guitar broke.
senses.exampleCN: 吉他的一根弦断了。
senses.why: Sound is made by a stretched cord.
senses.whyCN: 声音由绷紧的弦发出。

intro.en: String comes from Old English streng, a cord.
intro.cn: string 来自古英语 streng，意为绳。

items.en: Streng meant a cord or rope.
items.cn: streng 指绳或索。

items.en: The root named a twisted line.
items.cn: 这个词根表示搓成的线。

items.en: String named a thin cord.
items.cn: 中古英语 string 指细绳。

items.en: A string of things meant a series.
items.cn: a string of things 表示一连串事物。

items.en: Instrument strings gave string its musical sense.
items.cn: 乐器上的弦赋予了 string 音乐含义。

note.en: String is compared with look-alike words and with words for cord.
note.cn: 把 string 与形近词以及表示绳线的词作比较。

entries.definition: a very thin line of cotton

normalIntro.en: String is a line that ties, lines up, or sings.
normalIntro.cn: string 是一根能捆、能串、能唱的线。

normal.en: She cut the string with scissors.
A string of buses waited outside.
He plays a string instrument.
She pulled strings to get the job.
normal.cn: 她走后门得到了这份工作。

normal.en: They offered help with no strings attached.
normal.cn: 他们提供帮助，不附带条件。

abstract.en: A string is a promise stretched between two points.
abstract.cn: 一根绳，是两点之间拉紧的承诺。

abstract.en: Small things become a story when strung together.
abstract.cn: 小东西串起来，就成了故事。

abstract.en: Even a thin string can make a sound.
abstract.cn: 再细的弦，也能发出声音。

examples.en: She tied the parcel with a piece of string.
examples.cn: 她用一根细绳把包裹捆好。

examples.en: A string of lights hung across the street.
examples.cn: 一串灯横挂在街道上方。

examples.en: One string of the guitar broke.
examples.cn: 吉他的一根弦断了。

dict_mnemonic.text: string 是「细绳」；把东西串在绳上成了一串，把绳绷在乐器上成了弦，暗地里牵绳就是走后门。

root: 来自古英语 streng（绳、索），属日耳曼语词，本指搓成的线；由实物的细绳，引申为一串事物，再指乐器上发声的弦。

sensesIntro.en: String is cord you tie with, a row of things, or a cord that sings.
sensesIntro.cn: string 是拿来捆的绳、排成一串的东西，或会唱歌的弦。

core.en: A thin line pulled through a parcel.
core.cn: 一根穿过包裹的细线。

branches.en: A parcel is tied shut.
branches.cn: 包裹被捆好。

branches.en: Lights hang one after another.
branches.cn: 灯一盏接一盏地挂着。

branches.en: A finger presses a guitar string.
branches.cn: 手指按住吉他弦。

branches.en: The cord turns separate things into a row.
branches.cn: 绳子把分散的东西变成一列。

branches.en: A row of notes hangs on a string.
branches.cn: 一串音符挂在弦上。

intro.en: String forms a plural and adjectives about texture and music.
intro.cn: string 有复数，并能构成表示质地与音乐的形容词。

latinIntro.en: There is no Latin root; the word is Germanic.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词没有拉丁词根，属于日耳曼语来源。

items.example: A harp is a stringed instrument.
The violin is a string instrument.
He pulled strings for his son.
The gift had no strings attached.

definition_en: to remove a covering or clothing, to take something away from someone, or a long narrow piece
core_image: 一层外皮被从上往下撕开，露出里面的东西
scene: 他脱掉湿衣服。He stripped off his wet clothes.
sceneCN: 这里 strip 是「脱去」（第 1 个义项）；句意：他脱掉湿衣服。

senses.title: Remove a covering
senses.definition: to take off clothes or a covering
senses.definitionCN: 脱去衣服或去掉覆盖物
senses.example: He stripped off his wet clothes.
senses.exampleCN: 他脱掉湿衣服。
senses.why: This is the physical removal.
senses.whyCN: 这是身体上的去除。

senses.title: Take something away
senses.definition: to take away power, rights, or possessions
senses.definitionCN: 夺走权力、权利或财物
senses.example: The court stripped him of his title.
senses.exampleCN: 法庭剥夺了他的头衔。
senses.why: Rights can be peeled away like clothes.
senses.whyCN: 权利也能像衣服一样被剥掉。

senses.title: A narrow piece
senses.definition: a long narrow piece of something
senses.definitionCN: 又长又窄的一块东西
senses.example: A strip of land runs along the river.
senses.exampleCN: 一条狭长的土地沿河延伸。
senses.why: A peeled layer can become a band.
senses.whyCN: 被剥下的一层，可以成为一条带子。

items.en: Strip also meant to remove a layer.

items.en: It came to mean taking away rights.
items.cn: 它开始表示剥夺权利。

items.en: A strip became a long narrow piece.
items.cn: a strip 指一条狭长之物。

note.en: Strip is compared with look-alike words and with words for removing.

normalIntro.en: Strip is a layer coming off, and what is left when it does.
normalIntro.cn: strip 是一层被去掉，也是去掉之后剩下的东西。

normal.en: He stripped the old paint off.
They stripped him of his rank.
A narrow strip of grass lined the road.
normal.cn: 路边有一条窄窄的草地。

normal.en: She read the comic strip in the paper.
normal.cn: 她读报纸上的连环漫画。

normal.en: The engine was stripped down for repair.

abstract.en: To strip is to find out what is underneath.
abstract.cn: 剥去，就是看看下面还有什么。

abstract.en: What is stripped away can be put back.
abstract.cn: 被剥掉的东西，还能装回去。

abstract.en: A thin strip is enough to mark a border.
abstract.cn: 窄窄一条，就足以标出边界。

examples.en: He stripped off his wet clothes.
examples.cn: 他脱掉湿衣服。

examples.en: The court stripped him of his title.
examples.cn: 法庭剥夺了他的头衔。

examples.en: A strip of land runs along the river.
examples.cn: 一条狭长的土地沿河延伸。

dict_mnemonic.text: strip 的核心是「去掉外层」；脱衣是脱去，剥漆是剥去，夺走头衔是剥夺，而剥下来的一条就是条带。

root: 来自中古英语 strippen（脱衣），与日耳曼语相关词同源；由去掉衣物与覆盖层，引申为剥夺权利，再由剥下的一层引申为条状物。

sensesIntro.en: Strip removes clothes or layers, takes away what someone has, or names a narrow band.
sensesIntro.cn: strip 去掉衣服或外层，夺走某人拥有的东西，也指一条窄带。

core.en: A layer peeled back from the top.
core.cn: 一层东西从顶部被剥开。

branches.en: Wet clothes fall to the floor.
branches.cn: 湿衣服落到地上。

branches.en: A title is taken away.
branches.cn: 一个头衔被拿走。

branches.en: A narrow field follows the river.
branches.cn: 一条窄田沿着河走。

branches.en: Clothes and honours can both be stripped.
branches.cn: 衣服与荣誉都可能被剥走。

branches.en: What is peeled off is itself a strip.
branches.cn: 被剥下来的东西，本身就是一条。

intro.en: Strip takes verb endings and builds adjective and noun forms.
intro.cn: strip 加动词词尾，并构成形容词与名词。

latinIntro.en: There is no Latin root; the word is Germanic.

definition_en: a long narrow band of colour, a band on a uniform, or a kind or type of person
core_image: 斑马身上黑白相间的一道道长纹
scene: 斑马的条纹黑白相间。A zebra's stripes are black and white.
sceneCN: 这里 stripe 是「条纹」（第 1 个义项）；句意：斑马的条纹黑白相间。

senses.title: A band of colour
senses.definition: a long narrow band of colour different from what is around it
senses.definitionCN: 与周围颜色不同的一条窄带
senses.example: A zebra's stripes are black and white.

senses.why: This is the pattern you see.

senses.title: A mark of rank
senses.definition: a band worn on a uniform to show rank

senses.example: The sergeant has three stripes.

senses.why: A band of cloth becomes a mark of standing.
senses.whyCN: 一条布带成了身份的标记。

senses.title: A type of person
senses.definition: a kind or group, as in people of all stripes
senses.definitionCN: 某种类型或群体，如各种类型的人
senses.example: The club welcomes people of all stripes.
senses.exampleCN: 这个俱乐部欢迎各种各样的人。
senses.why: Different stripes mark different kinds.

intro.en: Stripe comes from Middle English stripe, a band of colour.
intro.cn: stripe 来自中古英语 stripe，指一条色带。

items.en: Stripe named a narrow band.
items.cn: stripe 指一条窄带。

items.en: Related words named a line or stroke.

items.en: Stripe described patterns on cloth and animals.

note.en: Stripe is compared with look-alike words and with words for lines and bands.

entries.definition: a long thin mark of colour

normalIntro.en: Stripe is a line of colour, a line of rank, or a line between kinds.
normalIntro.cn: stripe 是一道颜色的线、一道身份的线，或区分类型的线。

normal.en: Writers of all stripes attended.

sensesIntro.en: Stripe is a band of colour, a mark of rank, or a label for a kind of person.

branches.en: A zebra crosses the road.

branches.en: A sleeve carries three bands.

definition_en: a sudden illness in the brain, a gentle movement of the hand, a single movement in swimming, or a single hit
core_image: 一只手顺着猫背轻轻滑过，动作平缓而连续
scene: 他轻轻抚摸猫的背。He stroked the cat's back gently.

senses.example: Her grandfather had a stroke last year.

abstract.en: The same word holds a touch and a blow.

abstract.en: One stroke of luck can change a whole year.

examples.cn: 他轻轻抚摸猫的背。

examples.en: Her grandfather had a stroke last year.

definition_zh: 结构的；结构性的；建筑承重构造的；系统深层的
definition_en: relating to the structure or framework of something, especially to its load-bearing parts or its underlying organization
core_image: 一座桥的钢架剖面被抽掉一块，周围的梁柱仍把重量一步步传向地基
scene: 这里指「结构的」。 The survey found structural damage beneath the bridge deck.
sceneCN: 这里 structural 是「结构上的、承重构造的」（第 2 个义项：与建筑的梁柱和承重体系有关）；句意：检测发现桥面下方存在结构损伤。图中可辨识物件：钢梁、桥墩、裂缝、承重箭头。

pos.zh: 结构的；结构性的；建筑承重构造的；系统深层的

derivatives.zh: 结构主义者；结构主义的

senses.title: Relating to a framework
senses.definition: relating to the way the parts of something are arranged and connected to form a whole
senses.definitionCN: 与某物各部分如何排列、连接成一个整体的方式有关
senses.example: The essay compares the structural features of the two novels.
senses.exampleCN: 这篇文章比较了这两部小说的结构特征。
senses.why: Latin structura named a fitting together, from struere 'to build'; the adjective therefore points to arrangement rather than to surface appearance.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁 structura 指「拼合、建造」，出自 struere「建造」；因此这个形容词指向排列方式，而不是表面外观。

senses.title: Load-bearing parts of a building
senses.definition: relating to the beams, columns, walls and foundations that carry weight and keep a building standing
senses.definitionCN: 与承担重量、使建筑站立的梁、柱、墙与基础有关
senses.example: A structural engineer approved the plans before construction began.
senses.exampleCN: 施工开始前，结构工程师批准了图纸。
senses.why: This engineering sense is the concrete core of the metaphor: the parts that bear load are literally the structure, and damage to them threatens the whole.
senses.whyCN: 这一工程义项是比喻的具体核心：承重的部件就是字面意义上的结构，它们的损伤会威胁整体。

senses.title: Of a language as a system
senses.titleCN: 语言学中的结构：把语言视为系统
senses.definition: in linguistics, describing language as a system of relations among sounds, words and sentences rather than as a list of items
senses.definitionCN: 在语言学中，把语言描述为声音、词与句子之间的关系系统，而不是一份条目清单
senses.example: Structural analysis shows that the two dialects share the same sound system.
senses.exampleCN: 结构分析显示，这两种方言共享同一套语音系统。
senses.why: Twentieth-century linguistics shifted attention from isolated words to the network that holds them together, and structural became the label for that viewpoint.
senses.whyCN: 二十世纪语言学把关注点从孤立的词转向维系它们的网络，structural 成为这一视角的标签。

senses.title: Underlying causes in a system
senses.definition: describing a cause that lies in the organization of a system rather than in the choices of one person
senses.definitionCN: 指某项原因存在于系统的组织方式中，而不是某个人的选择中
senses.example: Poverty in the region is structural, not a matter of individual effort.
senses.exampleCN: 该地区的贫困是结构性的，与个人努力无关。
senses.why: If the arrangement of institutions produces the outcome, blaming individuals misses the mechanism; structural names that mechanism and is often opposed to personal or accidental.
senses.whyCN: 如果制度安排产生了这一结果，归咎个人就错失了机制；structural 命名这一机制，常与「个人的」「偶然的」相对。

senses.title: Change that alters the framework
senses.titleCN: 改变框架本身的结构性变革
senses.definition: describing reform or change that alters the basic organization of an economy, industry or institution rather than adjusting its surface
senses.definitionCN: 指改变经济、产业或机构基本组织方式的改革，而不是表面调整
senses.example: The country undertook structural reforms in taxation and labour law.
senses.exampleCN: 该国在税制与劳动法方面进行了结构性改革。
senses.why: Policy language distinguishes a structural reform from a temporary fix: the former changes the rules that generate outcomes, not just the outcomes themselves.
senses.whyCN: 政策语言把结构性改革与临时补救区分开：前者改变产生结果的规则，而不只是结果本身。

senses.title: Arrangement of molecules or cells
senses.titleCN: 分子或细胞层面的结构
senses.definition: in chemistry and biology, relating to the arrangement of atoms, molecules or tissues and how that arrangement determines function
senses.definitionCN: 在化学与生物学中，与原子、分子或组织的排列方式以及该排列如何决定功能有关
senses.example: Structural biology revealed how the protein binds its target.
senses.exampleCN: 结构生物学揭示了这种蛋白质如何结合靶点。
senses.why: Function follows form at the molecular scale: knowing how the parts are arranged explains what the molecule can do, which is why the adjective attaches to biology.
senses.whyCN: 在分子尺度上功能随形式而来：了解各部分如何排列，就能解释分子能做什么，因此这个形容词常与生物学搭配。

senses.title: Inequality built into society
senses.titleCN: 制度化的结构性不平等
senses.definition: describing disadvantage that is reproduced by the rules, norms and organization of a society rather than by individual prejudice alone
senses.definitionCN: 指由社会的规则、规范与组织方式不断再生产出来的不利处境，而非仅由个人偏见造成
senses.example: The report documented structural inequality in housing and schooling.
senses.exampleCN: 报告记录了指住房与教育方面的结构性不平等。
senses.why: This social sense extends the engineering image to institutions: the rules act as beams that distribute advantage unevenly, so the pattern persists even when individuals change.
senses.whyCN: 这一社会义项把工程意象扩展到制度：规则像梁一样不均匀地分配优势，因此即使个人更替，模式仍然持续。

senses.title: Damage to the load-bearing frame
senses.definition: describing physical damage that affects the frame or foundation of a building, vehicle or machine rather than its surface
senses.definitionCN: 指影响建筑、车辆或机器框架或基础的物理损伤，而不是表面损伤
senses.example: The earthquake caused structural damage but no injuries.
senses.exampleCN: 地震造成了结构损伤，但无人受伤。
senses.why: This sense returns to the literal core: cosmetic cracks can be repaired, but structural damage means the part that carries the load is compromised, so the whole is at risk.
senses.whyCN: 这一义项回到字面核心：表面裂缝可以修补，而结构损伤意味着承重部件受损，整体因而处于风险中。

intro.en: Structural is structure plus the adjective ending -al; structure comes from Latin structura 'a building, a fitting together', from struere 'to build, pile up'. The deeper root is reconstructed.
intro.cn: structural 是 structure 加形容词词尾 -al；structure 出自拉丁 structura「建筑、拼合」，源自 struere「建造、堆叠」。其更深词根为重构形式。

items.en: Latin struere meant 'to build, pile up, arrange', and its past participle structus supplied the notion of something already built. The deeper root is reconstructed as Indo-European *streu- 'to spread, pile up'.
items.cn: 拉丁 struere 意为「建造、堆叠、安排」，其过去分词 structus 提供「已建成之物」的概念。更深词根被重构为印欧语 *streu-「铺开、堆积」。

items.en: Structura named the act of building and the building itself, hence 'a fitting together, an arrangement'. It is the direct source of English structure.
items.cn: structura 指建造行为及建筑物本身，因而表示「拼合、安排」。它是英语 structure 的直接来源。

items.en: English borrowed structure in the fifteenth century, first for buildings and later for the arrangement of any organized whole.
items.cn: 英语在十五世纪借入 structure，最初指建筑物，后来指任何有组织整体的排列方式。

items.en: The adjective structural appears later, formed on structure with -al, and spread in engineering, biology and grammar in the nineteenth century.
items.cn: 形容词 structural 出现较晚，由 structure 加 -al 构成，并在十九世纪扩展到工程、生物与语法领域。

items.en: Twentieth-century linguistics and anthropology made structural a key term for systems of relations, giving the word its abstract, systemic sense.
items.cn: 二十世纪的语言学与人类学使 structural 成为「关系系统」的关键术语，赋予该词抽象的、系统性的义项。

items.en: First-attestation uncertainty: the earliest English citation of structural is unknown. Reconstructed form: the Indo-European root of struere, *streu-, is a reconstruction rather than a recorded word, and its exact semantic range remains disputed.
items.cn: 首见年代存疑：structural 的英语最早书证年代不确定。重构形式：struere 的印欧语词根 *streu- 属重构，并非有记录的真实词形，其确切语义范围仍有争议。

note.en: The first group separates the structure family by part of speech and use; the second gives near-synonyms for being fundamental to a system.
note.cn: 第一组按词性与用法区分 structure 词族；第二组给出表示「属于系统根本」的近义词。

entries.definition: The arrangement itself, or the act of arranging. Structural is the adjective describing it.
entries.definitionCN: 指排列本身，或安排的动作；structural 是描述它的形容词。

entries.definition: Having a definite plan or pattern. Structured describes a thing that was organized; structural describes what belongs to the frame.
entries.definitionCN: 指具有明确计划或模式；structured 描述被组织好的事物，structural 描述属于框架的东西。

entries.definition: The school of thought that analyses systems of relations. Structural is the adjective; structuralism is the doctrine.
entries.definitionCN: 指分析关系系统的学派；structural 是形容词，structuralism 是学说。

entries.definition: The adverb answering 'in what respect?'. Structural modifies a noun; structurally modifies a verb or adjective.
entries.definitionCN: 副词，回答「在哪方面」；structural 修饰名词，structurally 修饰动词或形容词。

entries.definition: Affecting the whole system rather than a part. It stresses spread through the system; structural stresses the framework that causes the spread.
entries.definitionCN: 指影响整个系统而非局部；systemic 强调贯穿系统，structural 强调造成这种贯穿的框架。

entries.definition: Relating to the art and design of buildings. Structural concerns whether they stand; architectural concerns how they are conceived.
entries.definitionCN: 指建筑艺术与设计；structural 关心建筑能否站住，architectural 关心如何构思。

entries.definition: Relating to the way a group is arranged. It is the social counterpart of structural, which can also describe beams and molecules.
entries.definitionCN: 指群体的安排方式，是 structural 在社会领域的对应词，而 structural 也能描述梁柱与分子。

entries.definition: Serving as the base or basis. It points to what everything rests on, while structural points to how the parts are connected.
entries.definitionCN: 指作为基础或依据，强调一切所依托之物；structural 强调部分如何连接。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real collocations and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: structure + -al: of the frame that holds the parts together.
normal.cn: structure + -al：属于把各部分撑在一起的框架。

normal.en: The family runs structure, structured, structuralism, structuralist, restructure, infrastructure.
Fixed phrases show the range: structural damage, structural reform, structural adjustment, structural engineer.
normal.cn: 固定搭配展示范围：结构损伤、结构性改革、结构调整、结构工程师。

normal.en: A structure carries load; a structural problem is one in the load-bearing part.
normal.cn: 结构承担荷载；结构性问题就出在承重部分。

normal.en: Structural causes outlast individual choices.
normal.cn: 结构性原因比个人选择更持久。

abstract.en: Picture a bridge cut open so the beams and the arrows of load are visible.
abstract.cn: 想象一座桥被剖开，梁柱与荷载箭头都可见。

abstract.en: Picture a building whose walls are rules rather than bricks.
abstract.cn: 想象一座建筑，墙体是规则而不是砖块。

abstract.en: Picture a skeleton inside a body, holding up everything that looks soft.
abstract.cn: 想象身体里的一副骨架，撑起所有看似柔软的部分。

examples.en: The inspection found structural cracks in three of the columns.
examples.cn: 检查发现其中三根柱子有结构裂缝。

examples.en: High youth unemployment is a structural problem, not a seasonal one.
examples.cn: 青年高失业率是结构性问题，而不是季节性问题。

examples.en: Structural biology maps the shape of proteins to explain their function.
examples.cn: 结构生物学绘制蛋白质的形状，以解释其功能。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「structure（结构）+ al」——看骨架，不看表皮 → structural 结构的

root: 拉丁 struere「建造、堆叠」→ 过去分词 structus → 拉丁 structura「建筑、拼合」→ 英语 structure + -al。更深词根为重构形式 *streu-。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses move from arrangement in general to load-bearing frames, language systems, underlying causes, framework-changing reform, molecular shape, social inequality and literal structural damage.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项从一般排列方式，扩展到承重框架、语言系统、深层原因、改变框架的改革、分子形态、社会不平等，最后回到字面上的结构损伤。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a visible frame carries weight from the top down to the base.
core.cn: 核心意象：可见的框架把重量从顶部一路传到基座。

branches.en: ARRANGEMENT AS SUCH: how the parts are put together to make a whole.
branches.cn: 排列本身：各部分如何拼合成一个整体。

branches.en: LOAD PATH: beams and foundations carry weight, and damage there endangers the whole.
branches.cn: 荷载路径：梁与基础承担重量，此处受损会危及整体。

branches.en: SYSTEMS OF RELATIONS: sounds in a language, atoms in a molecule, arranged so that form explains function.
branches.cn: 关系系统：语言中的音、分子中的原子，其排列使形式解释功能。

branches.en: CAUSES BUILT INTO INSTITUTIONS: outcomes reproduced by rules rather than by individual choice.
branches.cn: 制度内置的原因：结果由规则而非个人选择不断再生产。

branches.en: REFORM AT THE FRAME: change the rules that generate outcomes, not just the outcomes.
branches.cn: 框架层面的改革：改变产生结果的规则，而不只是结果。

intro.en: Structural is a Latin-derived base plus an adjective ending: struere 'to build' gives structura, English structure, and then structural with -al.
intro.cn: structural 是拉丁词基加形容词词尾：struere「建造」给出 structura，英语作 structure，再加 -al 成为 structural。

latinIntro.en: Latin struere and structura also underlie construct, destruction, instruct, obstruct and infrastructure, all built on the image of piling parts into a frame.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 struere 与 structura 也支撑 construct、destruction、instruct、obstruct、infrastructure，都建立在「把部件堆成框架」的意象上。

items.example: The two buildings are structurally similar.

items.meaning: to organize again in a new way

items.meaning: the underlying systems a society needs
items.meaningCN: 社会所依赖的基础系统
items.example: Roads and water pipes are infrastructure.
items.exampleCN: 道路与水管属于基础设施。

items.meaning: the supporting part beneath a building
items.meaningCN: 建筑物下方的支撑部分

definition_en: the way parts are arranged and joined, an organized system, or to arrange something in a planned way
core_image: 一座建筑的梁柱彼此咬合，撑起整体形状
scene: 这座桥的结构非常坚固。The structure of the bridge is very solid.
sceneCN: 这里 structure 是「结构」（第 1 个义项）；句意：这座桥的结构非常坚固。

senses.title: How parts are joined
senses.definition: the way the parts of something are arranged and joined
senses.definitionCN: 事物各部分排列与连接的方式
senses.example: The structure of the bridge is very solid.
senses.exampleCN: 这座桥的结构非常坚固。
senses.why: This is the shape held by parts.
senses.whyCN: 这是各部分撑起来的形状。

senses.title: An organized system
senses.definition: a system of parts that work together, as in society
senses.definitionCN: 各部分协同运作的体系，如社会
senses.example: The village has a simple social structure.
senses.exampleCN: 这个村子有简单的社会结构。
senses.why: Buildings and societies are both built.
senses.whyCN: 建筑与社会都是「搭」起来的。

senses.title: Arrange on purpose
senses.definition: to arrange something in a planned way
senses.definitionCN: 有计划地安排某事物
senses.example: She structured the report around three questions.
senses.exampleCN: 她围绕三个问题来组织这份报告。
senses.why: The noun becomes the act of building it.
senses.whyCN: 名词在这里变成了搭建的动作。

intro.en: Structure comes from Latin structura, a fitting together.
intro.cn: structure 来自拉丁语 structura，意为拼合、建造。

items.en: Structura meant building or arrangement.
items.cn: structura 意为建造或排列。

items.en: Struere meant to pile up or build.
items.cn: struere 意为堆起或建造。

items.en: Structure named a building's frame.
items.cn: 中古英语 structure 指建筑的骨架。

items.en: It described the parts of a whole.
items.cn: 它开始描述整体的各部分。

items.en: It also became a verb meaning to arrange.
items.cn: 它也变成动词，表示安排组织。

note.en: Structure is compared with look-alike words and with words for frameworks.
note.cn: 把 structure 与形近词以及表示框架的词作比较。

normalIntro.en: Structure is the order that holds parts together.
normalIntro.cn: structure 是把各部分拢在一起的那份秩序。

normal.en: The structure of the cell is simple.
normal.cn: 这个细胞的结构很简单。

normal.en: Social structure shapes daily life.
normal.cn: 社会结构塑造着日常生活。

normal.en: Check the sentence structure again.
They restructured the company.
She structured her speech clearly.
normal.cn: 她把演讲组织得很清楚。

abstract.en: Structure is a promise that parts will meet.
abstract.cn: 结构，是各部分终会相遇的承诺。

abstract.en: Remove one beam and the whole shape changes.
abstract.cn: 抽掉一根梁，整个形状就变了。

abstract.en: We build structures, and structures build us.
abstract.cn: 我们建造结构，结构也塑造我们。

examples.en: The structure of the bridge is very solid.
examples.cn: 这座桥的结构非常坚固。

examples.en: The village has a simple social structure.
examples.cn: 这个村子有简单的社会结构。

examples.en: She structured the report around three questions.
examples.cn: 她围绕三个问题来组织这份报告。

dict_mnemonic.text: structure 来自「建造」；梁柱怎么搭是结构，人与人的位置怎么排是体系，把事情按顺序搭好就是构建。

root: 来自拉丁语 structura（建造、拼合），源于 struere（堆起、建造）；由建筑的骨架，引申为事物各部分的组织方式，再扩大到社会体系与动词「构建」。

sensesIntro.en: Structure is how parts fit, a system of parts, or the act of arranging them.
sensesIntro.cn: structure 是各部分如何拼合、由部分组成的体系，或把部分安排好的动作。

core.en: Beams meeting at a firm joint.
core.cn: 梁木在牢固的接点相遇。

branches.en: A bridge holds its shape.
branches.cn: 桥保持着形状。

branches.en: A village arranges its roles.
branches.cn: 村子安排着各自的角色。

branches.en: A writer orders three points.
branches.cn: 作者排出三个要点。

branches.en: A frame of wood and a frame of roles both hold.
branches.cn: 木头的框架与角色的框架，都能撑住。

branches.en: To structure is to choose an order.
branches.cn: 构建，就是选择一种顺序。

intro.en: Structure takes verb endings and builds adjective and verb forms.
intro.cn: structure 加动词词尾，并构成形容词与动词。

latinIntro.en: The Latin root is struere, to build, giving structura.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁词根是 struere（建造），名词为 structura。

definition_en: to fight hard against difficulty, or a hard fight or effort
core_image: 一个人在水里拼命划动双臂，向岸边靠近
scene: 他在水里挣扎着游向岸边。He struggled through the water toward the shore.
sceneCN: 这里 struggle 是「挣扎」（第 1 个义项）；句意：他在水里挣扎着游向岸边。

senses.title: Fight against difficulty
senses.definition: to use great effort against something difficult or dangerous
senses.definitionCN: 为对抗困难或危险而拼尽全力
senses.example: He struggled through the water toward the shore.
senses.exampleCN: 他在水里挣扎着游向岸边。
senses.why: This is effort against a force.
senses.whyCN: 这是与一股力量对抗所花的力气。

senses.title: A hard fight
senses.definition: a difficult fight or a long effort
senses.definitionCN: 艰难的斗争或长期的努力
senses.example: Losing the job was a real struggle for her.
senses.exampleCN: 失去工作对她来说是一段真正的艰难。
senses.why: The verb becomes the thing endured.
senses.whyCN: 动词在这里变成了所承受的事情。

senses.title: Have trouble doing
senses.definition: to find something very difficult to do
senses.definitionCN: 觉得某事非常难做
senses.example: He struggles with math.
senses.exampleCN: 他学数学很吃力。
senses.why: The fight is now with a task.
senses.whyCN: 这时的对手变成了一项任务。

intro.en: Struggle comes from Middle English strogelen, to fight hard.
intro.cn: struggle 来自中古英语 strogelen，意为奋力搏斗。

items.en: The word's exact source is not certain.
items.cn: 这个词的确切来源并不确定。

items.en: Strogelen meant to fight or strive.
items.cn: strogelen 意为搏斗或奋力。

items.en: Struggle described effort against danger.
items.cn: struggle 描写与危险对抗的努力。

items.en: It also named a long hard effort.
items.cn: 它也指长期艰苦的努力。

items.en: Struggle with came to mean having trouble.
items.cn: struggle with 引申为做某事很吃力。

note.en: Struggle is compared with look-alike words and with words for fighting hard.

normal.cn: 那是为平等进行的长期斗争。

normal.en: He struggles with the new language.

abstract.en: A struggle is a door that does not open by itself.

abstract.en: What resists you also teaches you.

abstract.en: Small daily struggles build quiet strength.

examples.en: He struggled through the water toward the shore.
examples.cn: 他在水里挣扎着游向岸边。

senses.definitionCN: 艺术家或摄影师工作的房间
senses.example: The painter works in her studio.
senses.exampleCN: 画家在她的工作室里作画。
senses.why: This is a room made for making.
senses.whyCN: 这是一个为创作而设的房间。

senses.title: A production room
senses.definition: a place where films, music, or programmes are recorded
senses.definitionCN: 录制电影、音乐或节目的场所
senses.example: The band recorded the song in a studio.
senses.exampleCN: 乐队在录音棚里录了这首歌。
senses.why: Cameras and microphones need a controlled room.
senses.whyCN: 摄像机和麦克风需要一个可控的房间。

senses.title: A small flat
senses.definition: a small flat with one main room
senses.definitionCN: 只有一个主要房间的小公寓
senses.example: She rents a studio near the station.
senses.exampleCN: 她在车站附近租了一间单间公寓。
senses.why: One room serves for living and working.
senses.whyCN: 一个房间兼作起居与工作。

intro.en: Studio comes from Italian studio, a room for study or art.
intro.cn: studio 来自意大利语 studio，意为学习或创作之室。

items.en: Studium meant eager study.
items.cn: studium 意为热切的钻研。

items.en: Studio named a study or workroom.
items.cn: studio 指书房或工作室。

items.en: Studio named an artist's workroom.
items.cn: studio 指艺术家的工作室。

items.en: It moved into film and music production.
items.cn: 它进入电影与音乐制作领域。

items.en: It also named a one-room flat.
items.cn: 它也指只有一个房间的公寓。

note.en: Studio is compared with look-alike words and with words for workrooms.
note.cn: 把 studio 与形近词以及表示工作场所的词作比较。

normalIntro.en: Studio is a room where making happens, from paint to film to living.
normalIntro.cn: studio 是让创作发生的房间，从颜料到电影，再到生活。

normal.en: The artist cleaned her studio.
They built a new film studio.
normal.cn: 他们建了新的电影制片厂。

normal.en: The song was recorded in a studio.
He lives in a small studio.
normal.cn: 他住在一间小单间公寓里。

normal.en: The TV studio was full of lights.

abstract.en: A studio is a room that listens to its worker.
abstract.cn: 工作室，是一间听工作者话的房间。

abstract.en: One room can hold both a bed and a beginning.
abstract.cn: 一个房间，能同时装下床和起点。

abstract.en: Every finished work leaves a studio behind.
abstract.cn: 每件完成的作品背后，都有一间工作室。

examples.en: The painter works in her studio.
examples.cn: 画家在她的工作室里作画。

examples.en: The band recorded the song in a studio.
examples.cn: 乐队在录音棚里录了这首歌。

examples.en: She rents a studio near the station.
examples.cn: 她在车站附近租了一间单间公寓。

dict_mnemonic.text: studio 原指「钻研之室」；画家在里面作画是工作室，乐队在里面录音是录音棚，一个人住在里面就是单间公寓。

root: 来自意大利语 studio（书房、工作室），源于拉丁语 studium（钻研）；由艺术家的创作房间，扩展到影视与音乐制作场所，再指一室一厅的小公寓。

sensesIntro.en: Studio is an artist's room, a recording room, or a one-room home.
sensesIntro.cn: studio 是艺术家的房间、录制节目的房间，或只有一个房间的家。

core.en: A bright room with tools laid out.
core.cn: 一间摆好工具、光线明亮的房间。

branches.en: A brush rests beside a canvas.
branches.cn: 画笔放在画布旁。

branches.en: A microphone hangs from the ceiling.
branches.cn: 麦克风吊在天花板上。

branches.en: A bed and a desk share one room.
branches.cn: 床和书桌共用一个房间。

branches.en: Both art and sound need a controlled room.
branches.cn: 艺术与声音都需要一个可控的房间。

branches.en: A small studio can still hold big work.
branches.cn: 小小的工作室，也能装下大作品。

intro.en: Studio forms a plural and compounds for flats.
intro.cn: studio 有复数形式，并能构成公寓相关复合词。

latinIntro.en: The Latin source is studium, through Italian studio.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语来源是 studium，经意大利语 studio 进入英语。

items.example: The studios are on this street.
The art studio smells of paint.

items.meaning: a place where films are made

items.example: The TV studio has three cameras.
A studio apartment suits one person.
items.exampleCN: 单间公寓适合一个人住。

latinEntries.meaning: to learn, or a room for it
